newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-DEVILS, RED WINGS AND AVALANCHE WIN SERIES OPENERS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-DEVILS, RED WINGS AND AVALANCHE WIN SERIES OPENERS.

text.p: The New Jersey Devils, Detroit Red Wings and defending Stanley Cup champion Colorado Avalanche opened best-of-seven conference semifinal series with home victories on Friday.

At New Jersey, Martin Brodeur made 21 saves for his second consecutive playoff shutout and Scott Niedermayer scored a powerplay goal in the second period as the Devils claimed a tense 2-0 victory over the New York Rangers.

The Eastern Conference semifinal marks the first post-season meeting between the local rivals since their seven-game classic in 1994. That epic was won by the Rangers in the third game of the series to go to double overtime, propelling New York to the finals and the Stanley Cup.
Brodeur made six saves in the first period, eight in the second and seven in the third for his sixth playoff shutout.

Rangers goalie Mike Richter was also outstanding, keeping his team in the game with 32 saves. The Devils finally beat him on their 27th shot when Niedermayer wristed the puck through Richter's legs at 13:45 of the middle period with Esa Tikkanen in the penalty box for interference.
John MacLean sealed the game by scoring into an empty net with four seconds remaining.
"I think we played a solid game all around," Brodeur said. "We could have been ahead 4-0 in the first period except for Mike (Richter)."
New Jersey continued its perfect post-season penalty killing as the Rangers went 0-for-3 with a man advantage. The Devils have killed off all 19 penalties in six playoff games.
New Jersey dominated the first period, keeping Richter busy with 19 shots on goal to just six for the Rangers, but the New York goalie turned back every one.
Brodeur came up big with a series of stellar saves in the third period as the Rangers turned up the pressure.
"We can play better, we didn't play bad, but they earned the game, give them credit," said New York's Wayne Gretzky.
"We need more hunger going after the puck. We need more drive, more discipline and more intensity."

In Detroit, Martin Lapointe converted a picture-perfect cross-ice pass from Brendan Shanahan, easily beating goaltender Guy Hebert just 59 seconds into overtime as the Red Wings rallied for a 2-1 victory over the Anaheim Mighty Ducks.

Larry Murphy jarred the puck loose in the neutral zone and got it to Shanahan, who broke down the left wing, drawing Hebert to that side of his net as he prepared for a shot. Shanahan instead slipped the puck through Ducks winger Paul Kariya to Lapointe, who one-timed it into the open side of the net for the game-winner.
It was Lapointe's only shot on goal of the night.
The Red Wings had rallied to knot the game with just under nine minutes to go in regulation on a slap shot by Sergei Fedorov from the top of the right faceoff circle.
Kariya kept up his torrid post-season scoring pace, putting the Ducks ahead 1-0 with one minute left in the second period on a power play with his sixth playoff goal.
Kariya has been on the ice for 15 of the Ducks' 18 playoff goals.
Hebert finished with 28 saves, while Detroit goalie Mike Vernon turned back 19 shots.
In the other Western Conference semifinal at Colorado, Peter Forsberg had two goals and an assist and Patrick Roy made 35 saves as the Avalanche buried the Edmonton Oilers 5-1.

Joe Sakic had three assists and Sandis Ozolinsh and Eric Lacroix added a goal and an assist each for Colorado, which took advantage of a predictable letdown by the Oilers, who were coming off a stunning seventh game overtime shutout of the heavily-favoured Dallas Stars in the first round.
Sakic is the only player in the NHL to have points in every playoff game.
Claude Lemieux scored the other Avalanche goal, giving Colorado a 2-0 lead at 9:08 of the first period. Lemieux is tied for the NHL lead with six playoff goals.

Kelly Buchberger cut the deficit to one goal when he one-timed a bad clearing attempt by Roy into the net four minutes into the second period. But Forsberg restored the two-goal lead with his first of the night just under eight and a half minutes later and Colorado never looked back.
Edmonton goalie Curtis Joseph, who stole Game Seven from Dallas with an acrobatic save in overtime, was peppered with 37 shots and allowed all five goals.
Colorado, which beat Chicago in six games in the opening round, is 4-0 at home in the playoffs, outscoring the opposition 21-2.
